_comment: The comparison table's data. `site/tools/build.py` renders it and nothing else
writes it, which is the same split `content/ideas.json` has: data here, markup there.
Rules this file is held to, and `build_compare()` enforces every one of them:
- every row carries a cell for every tool, so a blank is impossible rather than
- every cell names at least one source id, and every source id is defined below;
- every defined source is cited by at least one cell, so a link cannot rot into
- `v` is one of yes | partial | no | unclear, and `unclear` is the correct answer
whenever the sources checked did not settle it. Guessing on a public comparison
is how one gets taken apart.
`checked` is the date every URL below was read. It is printed on the page, because
several of these projects move weekly and a comparison with no date is a claim about
2026-10-29: narrowed to the two closest tools (Orca and Herdr) plus tmux as the
baseline, and every cell re-read that day. Conductor, Superset and Warp were dropped
rather than left standing on sources read two months earlier.

herdr.t: Apache-2.0, for the TUI, the app and herdr-core.

rows.label: Runs on hardware you control, with nothing of the vendor's in the path

swemux.t: Local app data, with no swe-mux account, server or relay. The phone reaches your machine over your own tailnet. Providers and optional integrations still use the network.

orca.t: A desktop app on your own machines and subscriptions. The phone pairs over LAN or Tailscale, or through Orca Relay, a hosted relay in beta that needs an Orca sign-in.

herdr.t: Local binaries. Other machines join over SSH.

tmux.t: A local process, and nothing else.

swemux.t: None. The one request swe-mux itself makes is a daily update check, which the site counts as a constant label and an HTTP status, and which can be turned off.

orca.t: Anonymous usage events to PostHog Cloud (US), keyed to a random local ID. Settings, Privacy turns them off, as do DO_NOT_TRACK=1 and ORCA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1.

herdr.t: The app sends a daily report of versions and usage counts to telemetry.herdr.dev, on by default in release builds, never terminal text or prompts. Settings, Privacy turns it off.

swemux.t: The proving platform, and the one with a native desktop app and tray.

herdr.t: Stable-channel Windows x86_64 binaries; ARM64 runs them under emulation.

tmux.t: Windows only inside WSL or Cygwin.

rows.label: Desktop app on macOS and Linux

swemux.t: The daemon runs and the UI is a browser tab; CI starts a daemon from source on both. There is no desktop app for either.

orca.t: Apple silicon and Intel DMGs, and a Linux AppImage.

herdr.t: The TUI on both, and the app on Apple silicon macOS and Linux.

swemux.t: Five: Claude Code, Codex, pi, oh-my-pi and opencode. Any other CLI or shell runs unchanged in a real terminal, without the status layer.

orca.t: 41 in its supported-agents table, and it states it works with any CLI agent.

herdr.t: 23 detected, plus 4 that report their own state. Any CLI runs without a status.

tmux.t: None. It multiplexes terminals and does not read what is inside them.

swemux.t: Several signals combined: the CLI's hooks, its transcript, Claude's own session state file, the terminal screen and the process tree. Waiting names its reason (approval, question, rate limit, login), and idle with subagents still running is drawn apart from done.

orca.t: Terminal title sequences and agent hooks; for Claude Code, a status-line hook that emits OSC title events.

herdr.t: The TUI reads the screen against per-agent detection manifests, and uses an integration's own reports where one sends them. Its docs say Claude Code's and Codex's state come from screen detection.

swemux.t: The same application as an installable web app: the live terminal with a touch key rail, approvals, diffs, files, notes, the prompt queue, previews and push. No app store, login or relay.

orca.t: Native iOS and Android apps, which its docs call a read-mostly view of running agents: scrollback, short replies, source control, files, a browser view, account usage and push.

herdr.t: No first-party client. Its docs say to install any SSH client and run the TUI there.

rows.label: Your local dev server, opened on the phone

swemux.t: A server on the host's 127.0.0.1 opens in a Preview pane on the phone through swe-mux itself, hot reload and WebSockets included, with no extra port exposed.

orca.t: A Web or Mobile browser view from the phone; its docs say Mobile asks the paired desktop browser for a phone-sized viewport.

herdr.t: Links open in the default browser on the machine running the Herdr client.

rows.label: A built-in browser with developer tools

swemux.t: A Preview pane with refresh, page capture and live reload, and no developer tools.

orca.t: A Chromium window per worktree, with an address bar, DevTools and viewport emulation.

herdr.t: Links open in the host's default browser.

swemux.t: Claude and Codex accounts: 5-hour and weekly windows, history and resets, each window split into what swe-mux sessions used and what was used elsewhere. One-click login switching.

orca.t: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor and others: 5-hour, daily and weekly windows, multiple accounts, and cost estimated from a local price table.

herdr.t: Not described in the sources checked.

swemux.t: Full-text search across every recognized agent's conversations, a transcript view, resume from any result, and branching a Claude conversation from any message.

orca.t: Session History over about 22 agents' transcripts, filtered by title, directory, branch, model or text, with Resume.

herdr.t: Resumes 18 agents' native sessions after a server restart. Transcript browsing or search is not described.

rows.label: Per-session view of the tools, skills, MCP servers and hooks an agent can see

swemux.t: For Claude Code and Codex sessions, with where each came from and what changed after the CLI started. What the CLI can see, not proof a server connected.

orca.t: It reads each repository's .claude/ and .codex/ configuration; a per-session view is not described in the sources checked.

herdr.t: Lists its own integrations; a view of what an agent loaded is not described in the sources checked.

swemux.t: Every process and port is attributed to its session; ones still running after it ended, ones that escaped its tree, and heavy CPU or memory are flagged, with terminate-tree on a press. Nothing is killed automatically.

orca.t: A Resource Manager covering CPU, memory and sessions. Left-behind processes are not described in the sources checked.

herdr.t: Runtime status commands; resource use and left-behind processes are not described in the sources checked.

swemux.t: A supervisor separate from the daemon and the UI holds every terminal through a daemon restart and an app update, and typing keeps reaching them meanwhile. A reboot ends the processes; the sessions stay readable and resumable.

orca.t: A background daemon owns the terminals through quit, auto-update and a crash. A host reboot ends every running agent.

herdr.t: The app's agents keep running in herdr-core through quit, update and a crash. In the TUI a detach keeps them, and a server restart ends them and brings back the layout.

tmux.t: The server keeps sessions after every client detaches. Not across a reboot.

swemux.t: Worktree sessions, plus a land queue that merges a finished branch only after the check you approved passes, fast-forward only.

orca.t: Each agent runs in its own worktree.

herdr.t: Not described in the sources checked.

tmux.t: Out of scope. tmux knows nothing about git.
